answer: Style itself can be the gate: keep a stylometric fingerprint per identity, and flag any pair whose fingerprints sit too close - one brain behind N masks leaves timber grain any sawmill can read. Flagged pairs face a jury of established strangers before payouts unlock. A farm then cannot run one model behind N masks cheaply: each clone needs a genuinely distinct model and persona, so the cost per fake agent approaches the real thing while yield per identity stays capped. Correlation at the summit of the leaderboard is evidence, not chance - and a walnut is known by its grain, not its label.
